subject: SCIENCE
title: Light Lets Us See
objective: Distinguish sources and reflectors and explain safe seeing.
introduction: Milo turns on a lamp and sees a book because light reaches his eyes. How do sources and reflectors help us see safely?

vocabulary.definition: Energy that lets our eyes detect objects.
The star that gives Earth light and warmth.
A dark shape made when an object blocks light.

activities.instruction: Watch Milo trace light from a source to an object and eyes.
activities.content: We see an object when light from a source or reflected by the object enters our eyes. Never look at the Sun, lasers, or powerful lamps.

feedback.retry: Trace the light: a source makes it, an object reflects it, and eyes receive it.

activities.accessibilityAlternative: Text alternative: We see an object when light from a source or reflected by the object enters our eyes. Never look at the Sun, lasers, or powerful lamps.

activities.instruction: Tap each object and decide whether it makes or reflects light.

examples: a lamp makes its own light
a book is seen by reflected light

feedback.correct: Great! You found the examples for Light Lets Us See. 🔎
feedback.retry: For each object, ask whether it makes light or reflects light.

activities.accessibilityAlternative: A numbered list of the same examples is available for keyboard and screen-reader use.

activities.instruction: Sort each observation by whether it describes a safe source or reflector.

fits: a lamp makes its own light
a book reflects light into eyes
doesNotFit: The Moon makes its own visible light

feedback.correct: Great sorting! Your groups are correct.
feedback.retry: Check the source, reflection, and eye-safety clue in each observation.

activities.accessibilityAlternative: Tap an item and then tap a labeled category; dragging is optional.

activities.instruction: Choose why Maxine can see a book in a lit room.

options: Eyes send a beam into it.
Light reflects from it into our eyes.
The book is visible without light.

feedback.correct: Correct: Light reflects from it into our eyes.
feedback.retry: Light from the lamp bounces off the book into eyes, which is the seeing clue.

activities.accessibilityAlternative: All choices are visible text and selectable with TalkBack.

activities.instruction: Match each object with its role in helping us see.

pairs.right: reflects light so eyes can see it

feedback.correct: Great! You matched each example with its Light Lets Us See explanation. 🔗
feedback.retry: Match each object with whether it makes light or reflects it toward eyes.

activities.accessibilityAlternative: A list-based matching control replaces drag gestures.

activities.instruction: Order the steps for explaining how light reaches our eyes.

steps: Ask: does it make its own light?
Sort it as source or reflector — never look at the Sun.

feedback.correct: Great! You put the Light Lets Us See steps in order. 🎉
feedback.retry: Check the order: identify source, trace reflection, explain seeing, then choose safe viewing.

activities.accessibilityAlternative: Up and down buttons provide an alternative to dragging.

items.prompt: Milo turns on a lamp and looks at a book. Which statement about seeing is true?

options.text: The Moon makes its own visible light
We see when source or reflected light enters our eyes.
Eyes send light into every object.

items.explanation: Light from a source or reflected by an object enters the eyes, allowing us to see. The Moon reflects light, and staring at the Sun is unsafe.

items.prompt: Maxine sorts a lamp, shirt, book, and candle. Which pair names an object and its light role?
items.explanation: A lamp makes its own light, so it is a source. A shirt and book mainly reflect light, and darkness is not a light role.

items.prompt: Milo reads four statements about a lamp, Moon, and book. Which is NOT true?

options.text: The Moon makes its own visible light
A lamp makes its own light

items.explanation: The Moon shines by reflecting sunlight; it does not make its own visible light. A lamp is a source, and a book can reflect light.

items.prompt: A lamp shines on a book in Maxine’s room. Why can she see the book?

options.text: Eyes send a beam into it.
Light reflects from the book into her eyes.

items.explanation: Light from the lamp bounces off the book into Maxine’s eyes. Eyes receive light, and the book is not a source.

items.prompt: Milo sees his face in a mirror. Which pair correctly describes the light?

options.text: A book makes its own light

items.explanation: The mirror reflects light from Milo’s face toward his eyes, making the image visible. It does not make its own light or create the image from darkness.
